nbzinbKnight

nbzinbKnight fits two models for overdispersed count data, implementing the estimation from scratch rather than with a general-purpose optimizer:

  • Negative binomial (NB2) regression, nbreg(): iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for the coefficients, alternated with Newton–Raphson for log(θ). Same model as MASS::glm.nb().
  • Zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression, zinbreg(): an EM algorithm whose M-steps are IRLS fits (a logistic regression for the zero-inflation part and a weighted NB fit for the count part). Same model as pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin").

Both functions reproduce the reference implementations on the bioChemists and NMES1988 data (see the comparison tests in tests/testthat/). This package was written for the STA 651 final project.

Website: https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/, with the function reference and the project report.

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("knightrt-lgtm/nbzinbKnight")

Usage 

library(nbzinbKnight)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
fit_nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_nb)

# Zero-inflated negative binomial: count covariates | zero-model covariates
fit_zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                    data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_zinb)

# Model comparison and prediction
AIC(fit_nb, fit_zinb)
predict(fit_zinb, newdata = bioChemists[1:5, ], type = "zero")  # P(structural zero)

Both fits support print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik, AIC/BIC, fitted, residuals (Pearson and response), nobs, and predict. predict() for ZINB fits supports type = "response" ((1 − π)μ), "count" (μ), and "zero" (π).
